description: Save a secret that is not a login as a new secure note: a service account's key file, an API token, a licence key. Each secret goes in a field of its own, hidden by default, typed (value) or read from a file (file), with no password length limit: up to what Bitwarden stores in a field. Nothing returns the secret: the result names each field with its length, and a file's SHA-256 and size (compare them with the source's). get_field hands a value out; get_login names the fields. Filed into the account's own vault, outside any collection unless `collection` names another. If a call fails without saying whether the note was saved, find_logins by its name before trying again.

collection.description: A collection name from health. Default: the account's own vault, outside any collection.

fields.description: The secrets, one field each, and any plain details beside them.

file.description: The value from a file, taken whole and exactly: every line, a final line ending included (a JSON key file, a PEM key, a token). UTF-8 text up to 3695 bytes. Delete the file once the note is saved. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-8rxs9k8t), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

path.description: A path: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-8rxs9k8t); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

hidden.description: A hidden field is a secret: get_login names it without its value. Default true; false for a plain detail such as a project id.

name.description: The field's name, which get_field asks for, e.g. 'service account key (JSON)'. Names in one note must differ.

value.description: The value, typed exactly as you were given it. A secret that is already in a file goes as file instead, so it is never retyped.

name.description: What the secret is, e.g. 'Play service account key (example-app)'.

notes.description: Plain text anyone reading the note sees (get_login shows it): what the secret is for, where it is used. Never the secret itself.

name: create_note
title: Create secure note
